papers.title: Shank3 mutation disrupts the molecular signature of sleepiness across development.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used RNA-sequencing and polysomnography in Shank3 ΔC mice to examine how an autism-associated mutation alters the molecular response to sleepiness across development. The mutation blocked age-typical upregulation of neuronal growth and DNA repair pathways, while mutants persistently upregulated oxidative stress and protein synthesis pathways, impairing molecular responses to sleepiness.

papers.title: Baseline Dynamics and Sleep Loss-Driven Changes of Electrocorticographic Aperiodic Properties Are Altered in Mice Lacking Neuroligin-2.
papers.summary: Using Neuroligin-2 knockout mice and multifractal wavelet-leaders analysis of electrocorticographic signals, this study found increased Hurst exponent (Hm) across wake and sleep states, amplified daily Hm dynamics, and increased Dispersion in slow-wave sleep. Sleep deprivation altered Hm daily variations differently in knockout mice, and hypersynchronized epileptic-like events showed further Hm and Dispersion increases.

papers.title: Epigenetic characterization and manipulation of rare circadian neuron subtypes
papers.summary: The study developed Elution-based INTACT (El-INTACT) for high-purity nuclear purification and applied it to profile chromatin accessibility across six timepoints in ~120 Drosophila circadian neurons, including the 16 PDF-expressing LNvs. It identified a previously unknown Clk enhancer and used multiplexed CRISPR/Cas9 gRNA disruption to demonstrate functional specificity of distinct Clk enhancers.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals cell-type-specific circadian rhythms and their disruption by acute misalignment in mouse aorta
papers.summary: This study performed single-cell RNA sequencing of mouse aorta under aligned and acutely misaligned light-dark cycles, identifying cell-type-specific circadian rhythms and their disruption by misalignment. They found hundreds of cycling genes in vascular smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, with sex differences and molecular evidence of proteostatic stress after misalignment.

papers.title: Genetic ALS-Progressive Sleep Defects Precede the Onset of Clinical Disease.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal observational cohort of 18 presymptomatic ALS mutation carriers and 3 noncarrier relatives, polysomnography and EEG at baseline and follow-up (2.3 ± 1.5 years) showed that sleep macro- and microarchitectural alterations progressively worsened in all carriers. Progression appeared independent of proximity to motor onset, suggesting sleep measures as noninvasive surrogate biomarkers of premanifest ALS progression.

papers.title: Banxia Shumi Decoction Alleviates PCPA-Induced Insomnia and Regulates ADAM10 Expression via Melatonin Signaling in Rats.
papers.summary: Using a PCPA-induced rat insomnia model, this study showed that Banxia Shumi Decoction shortened sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration, with effects mediated via melatonin MT1/MT2 receptors. The decoction modulated sleep-related molecules CLOCK, PER1, CaMKII, GABARAP, mGluR1, and ADAM10, and these effects were reversed by the melatonin receptor antagonist luzindole.

papers.title: SEX-DEPENDENT MODULATION OF WHOLE BRAIN cFOS EXPRESSION BY LIGHT AND MELANOPSIN IN THE MOUSE
papers.summary: The authors generated a whole-brain atlas of light-induced cFos expression in mice, revealing broad activation beyond canonical visual circuits with strong modulation of neuromodulatory centers. Patterns differed between males and females and depended primarily on melanopsin-expressing intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells.

papers.title: Auditory stimuli extend the temporal window of visual integration by modulating alpha-band oscillations
papers.summary: In an EEG study, a brief auditory beep accompanying the first of two consecutive flashes shifted the psychometric fusion threshold to longer interstimulus intervals, indicating a wider temporal integration window. This behavioral shift was accompanied by a transient reduction in poststimulus instantaneous alpha frequency, and tACS and a phase-resetting model supported a role for alpha-band timing in audiovisual temporal integration.

papers.title: Personalized Brain Stimulation based on Brain Oscillations: A Systematic Review of MEG- and EEG-informed Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (tACS).
papers.summary: This PRISMA systematic review characterized the parameter space and outcomes of M/EEG-informed personalized tACS across 78 publications comprising 143 experiments, finding that 77.9% of sham-controlled experiments reported significant positive outcomes versus 56.2% with active control. Frequency-based individualization predominated (93%), most often targeting the alpha band (69.2%), with outcomes most commonly assessing physiological changes and cognitive functions such as perception and memory.

papers.title: Exploiting frontotemporal asymmetry in low-channel EEG emotion recognition via spectral fusion network.
papers.summary: The study introduced STSANet, a dual-branch spatiotemporal spectral asymmetric fusion network that explicitly models frontotemporal hemispheric asymmetry to decode emotions from low-channel EEG. STSANet achieved accuracies of 86.80% on the SEED dataset and 87.43% on a self-collected dataset, demonstrating robustness under cross-validation and highlighting the importance of spatial asymmetry modeling.

papers.title: A Neural Network with Multi-Type Attention for Enhancing Motor Imagery EEG Decoding.
papers.summary: The authors proposed MTANet, an end-to-end neural network with multi-type attention (EEG inception attention and parallel temporal sequence attention) to extract spatiotemporal-frequency coupling features from motor imagery EEG. MTANet achieved average accuracies of 83.39%, 89.47%, and 77.06% on BCI Competition IV datasets IIa and IIb and BCI Competition III dataset IIIa, respectively, outperforming seven state-of-the-art models.

papers.title: Clinical and Biological Characterization of Bipolar Disorder Patients With Chronic Insomnia Reveals Cortisol Reductions, Elevated TNF-α, and Increased Genetic Risk for Accelerated Aging.
papers.summary: This matched case-control study compared 22 bipolar disorder patients with chronic insomnia to 22 age- and sex-matched bipolar patients without insomnia, finding that the insomnia group had reduced waking cortisol, elevated TNF-alpha, and greater homozygosity for a TERT genetic variant linked to short telomere length and premature aging. Insomnia was independent of mood state, with a mean duration of 22.5 years.

papers.title: Sleep Variability From Routine Nursing Observation and Wearable Actigraphy for Early Risk Stratification in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients: Prospective Observational Study
papers.summary: Prospective observational study assessed whether early sleep instability during the first 7 days of hospitalization predicts prolonged length of stay in 94 acute psychiatric inpatients using wrist actigraphy and routine nursing observation. Greater actigraphy-derived sleep variability was associated with prolonged hospitalization (OR 2.42 per 1-hour increase; AUC 0.75), and nursing-derived sleep variability also carried independent prognostic information (adjusted OR 3.02; AUC 0.70).

papers.title: Transcranial rotating permanent magnet stimulation for focal continuous spike-and-wave during sleep: First-in-human pediatric pilot study.
papers.summary: This prospective, open-label first-in-human pediatric pilot study evaluated a single 10-minute session of transcranial rotating permanent magnet stimulation (TRPMS) targeted to the epileptogenic region in 10 children with focal continuous spike-and-wave during sleep. Sleep spike-wave index decreased significantly (90.6% to 81.7% and 85.3% to 77.0% for two blinded reviewers), with no serious adverse events, providing preliminary proof-of-concept for this nonpharmacologic neuromodulation approach.

papers.title: Observational Assessment of the Effect of Sleep Bruxism on Oxyhaemoglobin Saturation:A Preliminary Study.
papers.summary: In an observational polysomnographic study of 90 adults without obstructive sleep apnoea, individuals with sleep bruxism showed a significantly lower maximum oxyhaemoglobin saturation index compared with controls (p=0.04), while minimum and mean saturation did not differ. The difference was small and within normal physiological limits.

papers.title: The stems of Syringa pinnatifolia alleviate insomnia based on the brain-gut-microbiota axis mediated by 5-HT in mice and rats.
papers.summary: Using an equal mass to equivalent effect transmission (EMEET)-guided fractionation strategy in mice and rats, this study identified the phenolic fraction of Syringa pinnatifolia stems and its lignans alashinol F, alashinol G, and (-)-secoisolariciresinol as hypnotic constituents that shortened sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration. The effects were associated with decreased SERT and 5-HT2C/PLCβ1 expression, increased TPH and restored Gαq/11 expression, and altered gut microbiota including Bacteroidetes, Prevotella_9, and Blautia.

papers.title: Real-World Marijuana Use Is Associated With Altered Nocturnal Cardiac Autonomic Function, Reduced Sleep Quality, and Declining Consumption During Wearable Monitoring
papers.summary: In 16,965 wearable device users contributing 5.2 million person-days, within-person marijuana use was associated with lower nocturnal resting heart rate and heart rate variability, longer but more fragmented sleep, and an 11.1% decline in daily use probability over 72 weeks of tracking.

papers.title: Baihe Ganmai Dazao Decoction ameliorates depression-like and sleep-disturbance phenotypes: potential involvement of IL-17A/IL-17RA-related inflammatory signaling and microglial polarization.
papers.summary: This study optimized the compatibility ratio of Baihe Ganmai Dazao Decoction (BGMD) and demonstrated that it ameliorates depression-like behaviors and sleep dysfunction in CUMS/PCPA mice, potentially via modulation of IL-17A/IL-17RA signaling, restoration of microglial M1/M2 balance, and improved hippocampal neurotransmitter levels. Key active constituents and quality markers were identified.

papers.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea as a Driver of Venous Congestion, Cardio-Renal Dysfunction, and Cardiac Conduction Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.summary: This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence linking obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) to venous congestion, cardiorenal dysfunction, and cardiac conduction disease through mechanisms including intermittent hypoxia, sympathetic activation, inflammation, and fluid shifts. It highlights the clinical importance of recognizing OSA in these conditions, though many molecular pathways require further validation.

papers.title: Association between abnormal theta oscillation-default mode network functional connectivity and internet addiction behavior in adolescent depression patients: a resting-state EEG study.
papers.summary: This resting-state EEG study found that abnormal theta oscillation and default mode network (DMN) functional connectivity are associated with internet addiction (IA) in adolescent depression patients, with theta oscillation mediating the relationship between anhedonia and IA severity. The IA group showed lower theta power and distinct DMN connectivity patterns compared to MDD and healthy controls.

papers.title: Whose rhythms? Rhythmic agency, rhythmic justice, and circadian health in the menopausal transition.
papers.summary: This commentary introduces rhythmic agency (capacity to shape circadian-regulating conditions) and rhythmic justice (uneven distribution of that capacity) to reframe circadian disruption during the menopausal transition as a problem of social organization rather than individual behaviour. It outlines research directions and policy levers such as work scheduling, nighttime communication norms, urban lighting, and caregiving support.

papers.title: Vascular Bed Specificity in the Endothelial Link Between Sleep Deprivation and Hypertension.
papers.summary: This letter likely discusses vascular bed-specific endothelial mechanisms linking sleep deprivation to hypertension. No abstract was provided, so a detailed summary cannot be given.

papers.title: Neural Responsivity to Unexpected Stimuli Moderates a Developmental Pathway to Anxiety: A Community-Sample Replication in Early Infancy and Childhood
papers.summary: In 147 infants from a community sample, a more negative mismatch response at 4 months moderated the developmental pathways from high negative reactivity to behavioral inhibition and from high behavioral inhibition to anxiety symptoms at 30 months, with anxiety stable through 4-6 years.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging using a familial temporal lobe epilepsy model in cats: an exploratory methodological pilot study.
papers.summary: This exploratory methodological pilot study developed and evaluated simultaneous EEG-fMRI in cats with familial spontaneous epilepsy. While BOLD activation was detected in all sessions at an exploratory threshold, no activation survived multiple comparison correction, and individual-level epileptogenic zone localization remains insufficient for clinical use.

papers.title: Correlates of Multidimensional Sleep Profiles of Young Children.
papers.summary: Latent profile analysis of 320 Canadian children aged 1-5 identified two nighttime sleep profiles: Sleepy Koalas (59%) and Restless Raccoons (41%), with the latter showing shorter duration, later timing, longer latency, and poorer quality. Higher household income doubled the odds of Sleepy Koalas membership (OR=2.05), and in preschoolers, each unit increase in problematic parent-child sleep interactions reduced the likelihood of Sleepy Koalas membership by 21% (OR=0.79).

papers.title: Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound of the Amygdala in Depression and Anxiety: A First-in-Human Active-Controlled Trial
papers.summary: In a first-in-human, single-blind, active-controlled crossover trial, ten patients with major depressive disorder received amygdala-targeted low-intensity focused ultrasound versus somatosensory cortex control; amygdala sonication produced greater perfusion changes and resting-state connectivity reductions with a manageable safety profile, but symptom improvement did not differ between conditions.

papers.title: Sleep Duration and Sun Exposure in Portuguese Children: Associations With Obesity Indicators.
papers.journal: American journal of human biology : the official journal of the Human Biology Council
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 4755 Portuguese children aged 3-10, associations between sun exposure and sleep duration were examined with sex-stratified multiple linear regression. Modest sex-specific associations were found: in partially adjusted models, sun exposure was positively associated with sleep duration in girls and negatively in boys, but in fully adjusted models only a negative association for boys on Sundays remained (β=-4.57, 95% CI: -8.22 to -0.91).

papers.title: Illuminating Risk: An Ecological Analysis of Artificial Light at Night and Childhood Myopia Using State-Level US Data.
papers.summary: This ecological analysis of 2019 data from 46 US states used generalized additive modeling to examine the association between artificial light at night (ALAN) and childhood myopia prevalence. Higher ALAN was significantly associated with higher myopia prevalence (F=8.39, p=0.0068), with the final model explaining 65.3% of deviance; screen time showed a nonlinear relationship, and Medicaid coverage had a U-shaped association.

papers.title: Post-Stroke Recrudescence During the Perioperative Period: Potential Roles of Anesthetic and Sedative Agents.
papers.summary: Narrative review of post-stroke recrudescence (PSR) during the perioperative period, examining anesthetic and sedative agents as potential triggers. Evidence is strongest for benzodiazepines like midazolam, while evidence for other agents is limited; PSR is a diagnosis of exclusion and further prospective studies are needed.

papers.title: Venous Thromboembolism Risk Across Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery Subspecialties: A National Database Analysis.
papers.journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This retrospective national database study of 277,187 otolaryngology-head and neck surgery patients found an overall 90-day postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE) rate of 0.63%. VTE rates varied by subspecialty, being highest in head and neck (1.3%) and laryngology (1.0%), and highest among specific procedures such as free tissue transfer (6.1%) and lateral skull base surgery (4.4%); prior VTE was the strongest risk factor (OR=12.3).

papers.title: The role of air quality and pollution in obstructive sleep apnea: insights from recent studies.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes recent epidemiological and mechanistic evidence on the relationship between environmental exposures—including air pollution, indoor/outdoor pollutants, climate change, and meteorological factors—and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). It summarizes proposed biological mechanisms such as upper-airway inflammation, oxidative stress, autonomic dysfunction, and intermittent hypoxia, while noting that current evidence is heterogeneous and calls for standardized exposure assessment and longitudinal designs.

papers.title: Effect of modernized collaborative care for depression on individual depressive symptoms: A secondary analysis of the eIMPACT trial.
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of the eIMPACT randomized controlled trial (216 primary care patients) found that modernized collaborative care (internet/telephonic CBT and/or antidepressants) improved 15 of 20 SCL-20 items and 7 of 9 PHQ-9 items compared to usual care, with moderate-to-large effects on most symptoms but no significant advantage for suicidality, loneliness, sexual dysfunction, appetite change, or psychomotor symptoms.

papers.title: Sleep Quality and Daytime Sleepiness in Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in a Tertiary Care Hospital: An Observational Study
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 398 COPD patients, 52.78% had poor sleep quality and 46.23% had excessive daytime sleepiness, with both significantly associated with disease severity and exacerbation frequency.

papers.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea as a Modifier of Systemic Thromboembolic Risk Following Retinal Vein Occlusion.
papers.summary: In a retrospective matched cohort of 10,728 RVO patients per group, comorbid obstructive sleep apnea was associated with increased risks of anticoagulation initiation, venous thromboembolism, and myocardial infarction, but not arterial thromboembolism or stroke; among OSA patients, central RVO was linked to higher all-cause mortality than branch RVO.

papers.title: Effects of Progressive Muscle Relaxation on Sleep Quality, Serotonin, and Melatonin in Hospitalized Cardiac Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: A randomized controlled trial in 60 hospitalized cardiac patients found that progressive muscle relaxation significantly improved sleep quality and increased urinary 5-HIAA (serotonin metabolite) and 6-HMS (melatonin metabolite) levels compared to routine care alone.

papers.title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Multimorbidity: Insights from a National Claims Administrative Database.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: A cross-sectional analysis of Colombian national claims data (6,865,420 individuals) estimated diagnosed COPD prevalence at 2.21% and found significantly higher prevalence of multiple comorbidities, including asthma, sleep apnea, heart failure, ischemic heart disease, osteoporosis, and lung cancer, among those with COPD.

papers.title: A Four-Year Diagnostic Journey to Acute Intermittent Porphyria in a 19-Year-Old Woman: Lessons on Recognizing Neurovisceral Clues.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 19-year-old woman with a four-year diagnostic delay for acute intermittent porphyria, initially misdiagnosed with pseudoseizures, whose fecal total porphyrins were elevated (72.3 nmol/g) while plasma and urinary porphyrins were normal. The authors highlight that normal urinary ALA and PBG outside an acute attack do not exclude AIP and that fecal porphyrin analysis can provide complementary diagnostic evidence.

papers.title: Depressive Symptoms, sleep Disturbance, and Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity Among Adults With Arthritis: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of NHANES 2013-2020.
papers.journal: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2013–2020 data including 4,031 adults with arthritis, depressive symptoms and sleep disturbance were independently associated with higher odds of cardiometabolic multimorbidity, with sleep disturbance mediating approximately 15–19% of the association between depressive symptoms and CMM.

papers.title: Exploring Long-Term Outcomes in Sepsis Survivors: A Prospective Cohort Study Across Acute Hospitals.
papers.summary: A prospective longitudinal cohort study of 81 critical care-treated sepsis survivors across five Irish acute hospitals assessed long-term outcomes at 3, 6, and 12 months, following the Mid-German Sepsis Cohort protocol. The study found high rates of multidimensional impairment, with persistent fatigue, cognitive issues in over half, prevalent anxiety, depression, sleep disorders, and employment remaining below pre-sepsis levels at 12 months.

papers.title: ATS Core Curriculum 2026 Adult Pulmonary Medicine: Pulmonary Hypertension Diagnosis and Management.
papers.summary: This clinical review provides a comprehensive overview of contemporary practices for diagnosing and managing pulmonary hypertension in adults, covering right heart catheterization, risk stratification, treatment paradigms for pulmonary arterial hypertension, and management of specific subgroups such as chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. It serves as an evidence-based guide for clinicians and learners, emphasizing multidisciplinary care and supportive therapies.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
